clue.text: Men going on board with the wind up?

definitions.text: Men going on board with the wind up?

parts.words: Men going on board with the wind up?
parts.note: the 'men' are counters moved on a chequered board in a game, and the plural also names gusts of cold air, so 'with the wind up' suggests nervous sailors

explanation.surface: Frightened sailors climbing aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men going on board' reads like boarding a ship, but the men are game pieces on a chequerboard; the same word, plural, means cold currents of air.
explanation.definitionFit: The game played with round counters on a chequerboard shares its name with currents of cold air.

clue.text: His aim is to get the stock moving

definitions.text: His aim is to get the stock moving

parts.words: His aim is to get the stock moving
parts.note: stock sounds like shares on a market, but it is livestock driven along by a herdsman

explanation.surface: A trader trying to shift shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman drives cattle or sheep to market over long distances.

clue.text: Present for' cad due, to reform

indicators.note: to reform means the letters of cad due are formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A bounder is due a gift so he can mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or put forward evidence or an argument.

clue.text: Regular officer

definitions.meaning: usual or common, applying to most

explanation.surface: A soldier from the standing army who holds a commission.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means common or widespread, and also a top army commander.

clue.text: Soundly educated? Wrong!

indicators.note: Soundly signals that a word for educated is said out loud and spelt otherwise

parts.note: educated means taught

explanation.surface: Someone well-schooled turns out to be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, TAUGHT is said the same as the answer. 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Imprudent and awfully camp about sales-pitch

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
awfully suggests the word camp is done badly, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
an advertisement, AD for short, is a sales pitch

explanation.surface: A rash, overly flamboyant salesman's patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AD inside MCAP, the anagram of CAMP signalled by 'awfully'.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person acts wildly and recklessly, without thinking about the consequences.

clue.text: A little camphorated oil container

indicators.note: A little means only a small part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A small amount of camphor-scented oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little camphorated' looks like a quantity of oil; the jar sits inside CAMPHORATED.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-handled Greek or Roman jar held oil or wine.

clue.text: The film buff can see it, but not in its original form

indicators.note: not in its original form tells the solver the letters of can see it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A cinema lover can watch something, though not the original version.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is an enthusiast or connoisseur of the cinema.

clue.text: Puts on an act in front of nurses

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
tends means cares for, as a nurse does

explanation.surface: A performer acting in front of hospital staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to feign or make believe.

clue.text: 3's heraldic device

definitions.meaning: 3 down is the word for regular or common, so this is a synonym of that answer
in heraldry a simple broad charge such as a bend or chevron has this name

explanation.surface: A coat-of-arms emblem belonging to a numbered officer.
explanation.walkthrough: '3's' points to the answer of 3 down, GENERAL: the answer here means general, as in common.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary means commonplace, the same as general, and in heraldry it is also the term for a basic geometric charge on a shield.

clue.text: Used for washing no pegs needed

indicators.note: needed is the signal that the letters of no pegs are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Doing the washing without clothes pegs, as in a laundry note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a loose anagram signal here, perhaps sounding like 'kneaded': NOPEGS is rearranged. The surface suggests a washing line, yet the bath item needs no pegs to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft porous bath item is used to wash the body.

clue.text: Figure, the child among others is best off

indicators.note: among means these pieces sit amid the letters for others

parts.note: the rest means the others
I is the Roman numeral for one, a figure
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A youngster in a family photo who is better off than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I and CH inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthiest person is the one who is most well-to-do.

clue.text: Call for a replay

parts.note: reads like a referee's or captain's demand to replay a match, but means an audience shouting for a performer to play again

explanation.surface: A sports official demanding a match be played again.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience's cry for an extra performance at the end of a concert is this French-derived word.

clue.text: Giving guidance, an attendant takes in one group

indicators.note: takes in means the attendant swallows the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
I is the Roman numeral one
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: An attendant leading a party of people around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' puts I and LOT inside PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilotage is the act of steering or guiding, as of a ship through a harbour.

clue.text: Bill, the heartless rogue, will get time — a stretch

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of rogue are dropped, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A villain will be jailed for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the first and last letters of 'rogue', R and E. 'time' and 'a stretch' suggest prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an extent of land, a stretch of ground measured in acres.

clue.text: The bar lacked essentials — that's very bad

annotationWithheld.why: The bar lacked essentials — that's very bad (5-7): B + LACK(HEART)ED needs B from 'The bar' and a container signal; no word signals HEART going inside LACKED, and 'bar' as B is unsupported.
annotationWithheld.clue: The bar lacked essentials — that's very bad

clue.text: Make notes about a wine which is execrable

indicators.note: about means singing goes around the wine

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Writing tasting notes on a dreadful wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HOCK inside SING. HOCK is the British name for German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shocking is appalling or abominable, as bad as can be.

clue.text: Colours without point in an Oriental city

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the colours go around the point

parts.note: tints are colours
E is a point of the compass, east
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern city whose colours have no sharp edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: E goes inside TINTS, then IN follows. Tientsin is an old spelling of Tianjin in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Tientsin, now Tianjin, is a large port city in northern China.

clue.text: They operate on the head, though they're not brain surgeons

definitions.text: They operate on the head, though they're not brain surgeons

parts.words: They operate on the head, though they're not brain surgeons
parts.note: operating on the head suggests surgery, but it is styling and cutting what grows on top of the head

explanation.surface: A joke about medics who work on heads without operating on brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Salon workers cut and style people's locks, working on the head without any surgery.

clue.text: Person occupying the German housing in great style

indicators.note: housing means the German article holds the other piece inside

parts.note: der is German for the
well means in fine fashion

explanation.surface: A German living in a stylish home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' puts WELL inside DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is a resident or inhabitant of a place.

clue.text: Repeatedly let loose

definitions.meaning: to let or rent out again, read as a prefix for again plus a word for rent

explanation.surface: Freeing something over and over again.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to free, and split as re-lease it means to rent out once more.

clue.text: Counsel for a small daughter on failing

parts.note: D is short for daughter
a vice is a failing or moral weakness

explanation.surface: Legal representation for a young girl who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister, but it means guidance; 'for' and 'on' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance offered, the same as a recommendation on what to do.

clue.text: When fed-up scoff, that's best

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: When sick of something, gobbling it is best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED to DEF. 'best' is a verb here: to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, to overcome them.

clue.text: Gather a number on the roadside

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a number
taken as written
a verge is the grassy strip at a road's edge

explanation.surface: Counting cars parked by the road.
explanation.walkthrough: VERGE is the strip of grass beside a British road.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together at one point, as crowds or lines meet.

clue.text: Promise' quiet pupil some advantage

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
L is a learner, as on a driving L-plate
an edge is an advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A quiet student gaining a slight lead as reward for a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn vow or undertaking.

clue.text: The lady made off

indicators.note: off means the letters of made go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A woman left in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like 'went away', but it signals that MADE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dame is a woman, especially a titled or older one.

clue.text: Serving popular fish could be good for one's standing

definitions.text: could be good for one's standing

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sole is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Serving a trendy fish dish might improve one's social reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like social status, but it means standing on one's feet; 'Serving' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned inner sole inside a shoe helps comfort when on your feet.

clue.text: A periodical storage-place for military supplies

definitions.meaning: a regularly published journal or glossy paper
an arms store or ammunition depot, or the cartridge holder of a gun

explanation.surface: A journal kept in an army store.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a regular illustrated publication and a store for ammunition or explosives.

clue.text: Aristocrats demanding information before trial

parts.note: gen is slang for information
a try is a trial or attempt

explanation.surface: Upper-class people insisting on facts before a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'demanding' and 'before' only link the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed upper classes just below the nobility are the well-born social set.

clue.text: Opinion held about people, generally getting flats

indicators.note: about means the opinion goes around the people

parts.note: a tenet is an opinion or belief held
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk generally agreeing on flats as an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MEN inside TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into rented apartments, often run-down.
